subject: trouble storing results from normal_log() when vectorized

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: trouble storing results from normal_log() when vectorized
parts:
If I have the code:

    vector[2] a;
    vector[2] b;
    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b <- normal_log(a,0,1);

I get the parser error:

    base type mismatch in assignment; left variable=dummy; left base type=vector; right base type=real

If I change to:

    vector[2] a;
    real b[2];
    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b <- normal_log(a,0,1)

I get another parser error:

    mismatched dimensions on left- and right-hand side of assignment; left dims=1; right dims=0

I'm aware that I can loop over the indices of a to assign each element of b, but I'm of the (possibly mistaken?) impression from my R experiences that such loops are inefficient relative to vectorized approaches. This, however, presumes that a vectorized approach exists... does it? 

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trouble storing results from normal_log() when vectorized
parts: On Wed, Jun 26, 2013 at 12:25 PM, Mike Lawrence <mike....@gmail.com> wrote:

If I have the code:

    vector[2] a;
    vector[2] b;
    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b <- normal_log(a,0,1);

I get the parser error:

    base type mismatch in assignment; left variable=dummy; left base type=vector; right base type=real

If I change to:

    vector[2] a;
    real b[2];
    a[1] <- 1;
    a[2] <- 2;
    b <- normal_log(a,0,1)

I get another parser error:

    mismatched dimensions on left- and right-hand side of assignment; left dims=1; right dims=0

I'm aware that I can loop over the indices of a to assign each element of b, but I'm of the (possibly mistaken?) impression from my R experiences that such loops are inefficient relative to vectorized approaches. This, however, presumes that a vectorized approach exists... does it?

The issue is that the return of normal_log(a, 0, 1) is going to be real. A single value. In this case, the return of:
normal_log(a,0,1)

is equivalent to:
normal_log(a[1],0,1) + normal_log(a[2],0,1)

Hopefully that clears up the confusion.


What are you trying to do? If you want to store the unnormalized log of the normal pdf evaluated for each element of a, you could loop, but I'm not sure if that's what you actually want to do. From the modeling language, I don't think there is a way to ask for the normalized log pdf value for any of our distributions, so for this case, it will return -a[1]^2/2 - a[2]^2/2.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trouble storing results from normal_log() when vectorized
parts:
On 6/26/13 12:25 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> If I have the code:
>
> vector[2] a;
> vector[2] b;
> a[1] <- 1;
> a[2] <- 2;
> b <- normal_log(a,0,1);
>
> I get the parser error:
>
> base type mismatch in assignment; left variable=dummy; left base type=vector; right base type=real

The problem is that normal_log() returns a real, but b is a vector.
It adds all the log probabilities.

> If I change to:
>
> vector[2] a;
> real b[2];
> a[1] <- 1;
> a[2] <- 2;
> b <- normal_log(a,0,1)
>
> I get another parser error:
>
> mismatched dimensions on left- and right-hand side of assignment; left dims=1; right dims=0
Same problem, only for arrays.

> I'm aware that I can loop over the indices of a to assign each element of b, but I'm of the (possibly mistaken?)
> impression from my R experiences that such loops are inefficient relative to vectorized approaches. This, however,
> presumes that a vectorized approach exists... does it?

Unlike R, Stan is compiled. So basic loops, assignments, etc., are very
cheap. In fact, they're usually more efficient than the way R vectorizes
everything because you don't need to allocate temporary variables to
hold intermediate variables.

Having said that, you do want to vectorize calls to functions involving
parameters because the auto-diff is in some sense interpreted in Stan.
But given that normal_log returns a single log probability, there's no
alternative but to do a loop here.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] trouble storing results from normal_log() when vectorized
parts:
I'd try to get the model working first before worrying about
efficiency (reparameterization often helps with both).

You may run into overflow issues with all the exp().
You can use log_sum_exp() to carry out everything on
the log scale if you need to

The loop to set a zero vector can be replaced with
rep_vector(0,6), to create a 6-vector with all 0 values.

- Bob

On 6/26/13 2:21 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> Note: You suggested using rep_vector(0,6) in my transformed_data section (commenting out the for loop), but when I do
> so, I get a pretty low-level looking compile error. Possibly a bug?

Quite likely. Could you send along the error you get,
even if it's a novel.

The most likely cause would be an int/double incompatibility,
which if it's in the current release, has already been fixed
for 2.0. If this is the culprit, you could use
rep_vector(0.0, 6) instead of rep_vector(0,6).

- Bob
